subject: business_studies

concepts.title: Characteristics of Services
concepts.definition: The distinct behavioral and operational attributes that separate services from physical products, characterized by the five Is: intangibility, inconsistency, inseparability, lack of inventory, and customer involvement.
concepts.key_idea: Services are experiential, non-standardized activities performed in real-time with customer participation.
question_patterns: What are the five Is of services?
Explain the distinct features of services.
How do services differ from goods based on inventory and involvement?
Describe the nature of services with examples.

solution_steps.explain: The five characteristics are Intangibility, Inconsistency, Inseparability, Inventory (less), and Involvement.

Intangibility means they cannot be touched; Inconsistency means they vary per delivery; Inseparability means production and consumption happen together; Inventory-less means they cannot be stored; Involvement means the customer participates in delivery.

concepts.title: Types of Services
concepts.definition: The classification of services into three primary categories based on their target users and objectives: business, social, and personal services.
concepts.key_idea: Services are categorized by whether they support commercial activities, community welfare, or individual preferences.
question_patterns: Classify the different types of services.
What is the difference between business services and social services?
Define personal services with suitable examples.
Under which category do banking and tourism fall?

solution_steps.action: Categorize the service based on its primary objective
solution_steps.explain: Determine if the service is used for business operations (business), social upliftment (social), or personal enjoyment (personal).

concepts.title: Primary Functions of Commercial Banks
concepts.definition: The core financial services executed by commercial banking institutions, primarily consisting of accepting public deposits and lending funds.
concepts.key_idea: Banks act as financial intermediaries by borrowing from depositors and lending to borrowers.
question_patterns: What are the primary functions of commercial banks?
Explain how commercial banks accept deposits and lend funds.
Describe the different types of bank accounts available to depositors.
What is the role of commercial banks in credit creation?

solution_steps.explain: Banks accept funds through savings accounts, current accounts, and fixed deposits.
Banks advance loans via overdrafts, cash credits, term loans, and discounting bills.

concepts.title: e-Banking and Digital Payments
concepts.definition: The delivery of banking services and execution of financial transactions electronically over the internet using digital devices.
concepts.key_idea: e-Banking provides round-the-clock banking access, reducing transaction costs and physical branch load.
question_patterns: What is e-banking and what are its benefits?
Explain the different modes of electronic fund transfer.
How do NEFT and RTGS differ as digital payment methods?
What advantages does internet banking offer to customers and banks?

solution_steps.explain: Transactions are conducted via ATMs, EFT, NEFT, RTGS, or credit/debit cards.

solution_steps.action: Determine the benefits of the digital transaction
solution_steps.explain: Provides 24/7 access, transparency, and lower processing costs.

concepts.title: Principle of Utmost Good Faith
concepts.definition: The fundamental insurance principle (Uberrimae Fidei) requiring both the insurer and the insured to make complete and honest disclosure of all material facts.
concepts.key_idea: Non-disclosure of material facts by either party makes the insurance contract voidable.
question_patterns: Explain the principle of utmost good faith in insurance.
What happens if an insured hides a material fact from the insurer?
Define Uberrimae Fidei with an example.
Why is full disclosure mandatory in an insurance proposal?

solution_steps.explain: Verify if the proposer disclosed all critical details (e.g., medical history for life insurance, building structure for fire insurance).

solution_steps.action: Evaluate the validity of the contract
solution_steps.explain: If any material fact was concealed, the contract becomes voidable at the option of the insurer.

concepts.title: Principle of Insurable Interest
concepts.definition: The legal requirement that the insured must have a direct pecuniary or financial stake in the safety and preservation of the subject matter of insurance.
concepts.key_idea: The insured must suffer financial loss from the damage or destruction of the insured item or life.
question_patterns: What is insurable interest?
Explain the principle of insurable interest with examples.
When must insurable interest exist in life, fire, and marine insurance?
Can a person insure a neighbor's house under the principle of insurable interest?

solution_steps.explain: Check if the insured stands to suffer financially if the subject matter is damaged.
In life insurance, it must exist at inception; in fire, both at inception and loss; in marine, at the time of loss.

concepts.title: Principle of Indemnity
concepts.definition: The rule ensuring that the insurer compensates the insured only for the actual financial loss suffered, restoring them to their pre-loss financial position without profit.
concepts.key_idea: Insurance is meant for compensation of loss, not for making a profit; this principle does not apply to life insurance.
question_patterns: Explain the principle of indemnity.
Why is the principle of indemnity not applicable to life insurance?
How is compensation calculated under a contract of indemnity?
Show how indemnity prevents an insured from profiting from a loss.

solution_steps.explain: Indemnity applies to fire and marine insurance, but not to life insurance.
The compensation is limited to the actual loss incurred or the sum insured, whichever is lower.

concepts.title: Principle of Contribution
concepts.definition: The right of an insurer who has paid a full claim to recover proportional shares of the loss from other co-insurers covering the same risk.
concepts.key_idea: In double insurance, the insurers share the actual loss in proportion to the sum assured by each.
question_patterns: Calculate the contribution of each insurer in case of double insurance.
Explain the principle of contribution with a numerical example.
If a property is insured with two companies, how is the claim settled?
What is the formula for calculating proportional liability of co-insurers?

solution_steps.action: Sum the policy limits of all insurers
solution_steps.explain: Calculate the total sum insured by adding the individual policy limits.

solution_steps.action: Calculate the proportional contribution of Insurer A
solution_steps.explain: Divide Insurer A's policy limit by the total sum insured, then multiply by the actual loss.

solution_steps.action: Calculate the proportional contribution of Insurer B
solution_steps.explain: Divide Insurer B's policy limit by the total sum insured, then multiply by the actual loss.

concepts.title: Types of Warehouses
concepts.definition: The classification of storage facilities based on ownership, operation, and regulatory status, including private, public, bonded, government, and cooperative warehouses.
concepts.key_idea: Different warehouses cater to specific business needs, such as tax deferral (bonded) or cost-effective public storage.
question_patterns: What are the different types of warehouses?
Explain the utility of bonded warehouses for importers.
How do public warehouses differ from private warehouses?
Describe government and cooperative warehouses.

solution_steps.action: Identify the ownership and regulatory status of the warehouse
solution_steps.explain: Determine if the warehouse is owned by a private firm (private), licensed for public use (public), customs-controlled (bonded), state-owned (government), or run by a cooperative society.

concepts.title: Functions of Warehousing
concepts.definition: The logistical and value-adding operations performed by modern warehouses to facilitate smooth distribution, including consolidation, breaking bulk, stockpiling, and price stabilization.
concepts.key_idea: Modern warehouses act as dynamic logistics hubs rather than mere static storage units.
question_patterns: Explain the primary functions of warehousing.
How do warehouses help in price stabilization?
What is meant by consolidation and breaking bulk in warehousing?
Describe the financing and value-added services provided by warehouses.

solution_steps.action: Identify the specific logistical function performed
solution_steps.explain: Determine if the activity involves combining shipments (consolidation), dividing large shipments (break-bulk), seasonal storage (stockpiling), or packaging/labeling (value-added services).
